issues: Report-style defect: repeated “evidence boundaries” framing and cross-references to an “evidence boundaries” subsection reads like report-machinery/boundary narration rather than a polished bank disclosure section (deterministic pre-check failure).
Unsupported skills statement: the draft specifies climate-topic content and senior executive coverage for the skills development programme without compact evidence support.
Potentially unsupported implication of management committee continuity/evolution across years due to differing committee names in trend data.
unsupported_claims: “The governance structure includes … a management-level Climate Risk Management Committee …” (comparatives show different management committee names in 2022 and 2023; the draft does not acknowledge the year-specific naming and could be read as implying continuity/evolution).

“The Bank operates a skills development programme that includes climate-related topics for Board members and senior executives.” (skills development programme existence is evidenced, but inclusion of climate-related topics and coverage of senior executives is not evidenced in the compact evidence).

“The ESG & Sustainability Committee’s meetings include more detailed discussion of climate topics …” (committee existence and meeting frequency are evidenced; “more detailed” is an inference not directly evidenced).

“The Bank performed climate checks for major transactions in 2024, which complements the risk register and ERM integration indicators …” (the check itself is evidenced; “complements” is interpretive but not necessarily wrong).
material_unsupported_claims: Skills development programme scope/content claim: “includes climate-related topics for Board members and senior executives.” (Only programme existence is evidenced; content and audience breadth are not.)

Implied committee evolution/continuity risk: presenting the Climate Risk Management Committee as the standing management governance structure without clarifying that management committee naming differs by year (2022: Group Sustainability Committee; 2023: ESG Executive Committee; 2024: Climate Risk Management Committee).

minor_wording_to_tighten: “ERM integration indicators show that 6 of 8 … carry an ERM-integration flag.” (Tighten to avoid implying enterprise-wide ERM integration beyond the flag.)
“documented 2024 climate-related decisions” (acceptable, but avoid implying these decisions cover all material climate governance actions).

“principal controls and procedures supporting climate-related governance” (acceptable, but could be tightened to “key governance mechanisms” to avoid implying a formal control framework beyond what is evidenced).
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: “The Bank does not currently describe formal escalation thresholds for climate-related risks in this report.”
“The Bank does not currently publish a separate climate-specific charter, terms of reference or formal mandate for the Board or the ESG & Sustainability Committee.”
“Board decision records identify climate-related decisions but do not describe quantified or specific Board-level trade-offs …”
“The Bank does not currently describe a formal process for assessing the adequacy of Board climate skills beyond the reported indicators and skills development programme.”
Assurance limitation: limited assurance by EY under ISAE 3000 over Scope 1 and Scope 2 only; financed emissions outside scope; financed emissions figure used only for scope context.
Alignment limitation: TCFD/IFRS S2 alignment described as internal flags and not subject to a separate governance control process designed specifically to verify/assure alignment.
